newsitem.title: USA: Four jurors selected in du Pont murder trial.
newsitem.headline: Four jurors selected in du Pont murder trial.

text.p: Four jurors were chosen Tuesday as jury selection got underway in the murder trial of chemical heir John du Pont, accused of killing Olympic champion wrestler David Schultz nearly one year ago.

As a professional jury consultant hired by du Pont's lawyers looked on, Delaware County Court of Common Pleas Judge Patricia Jenkins and attorneys for both sides began questioning a pool of 75 potential jurors.
Three men and a woman were selected to sit on the jury by the time a late-running court session ended Tuesday evening. A total of 12 jurors and six alternates will be chosen.
Jenkins told the jurors they should be prepared for the actual trial to begin next Monday, and that the trial was expected to last about a month.
In her questioning of potential jurors, Jenkins indicated that du Pont's sanity, rather than whether he shot Schultz to death Jan. 26, 1996, would be the principle question in the trial.

"It appears that there may not be a dispute regarding whether or not Mr. du Pont physically perpetrated the act that resulted in the death of Mr. Schultz," Jenkins said. "It may be that the dispute underlying this case will be the mental state of Mr. du Pont at the time."

Major elements of her questioning focused on whether potential jurors had any biases regarding a defence of insanity, or whether they had formed fixed opinions on the case as the result of heavy media coverage.

Du Pont's lawyers have previously filed court documents saying they would pursue an insanity defence. Du Pont has been quoted as describing himself as the Dalai Lama and the Christ child, and previous associates have described a variety of eccentric behaviours by du Pont in the past.
Du Pont, 58, sat with his three lawyers in front of the courtroom, his drawn face framed by shaggy gray hair and a beard.
He wore a dark blue sweatsuit emblazoned in yellow with the name of the Foxcatcher wrestling team he sponsored at his estate in suburban Philadelphia, where Schultz was killed.
Schultz and his family lived on the Foxcatcher estate where he worked as a coach at a training facility.
Schultz's widow, Nancy, sat near prosecutors on the other side of the courtroom. She was expected to be present for the course of the trial.
In an initial screening round, the pool of 75 potential jurors was asked about issues such as any possible connections to du Pont or others involved in the case.

Males among the jurors chosen, who were not identified by name, were a 34-year-old Federal Reserve Bank employee, a 38-year-old computer worker and a 47-year-old commuter train conductor. A 54-year-old legal secretary was the only woman selected so far.
Du Pont, charged with first- and third-degree murder and related offences, faces an automatic life sentence if convicted of first-degree murder.
